hook.text: count plus plus broke because load and store were separate steps. What if the hardware did it all in one?

tas.text: test and set does. In one atomic step, it returns the old value of the lock, and sets the lock to true.

tas2.text: A process spins while test and set returns true. When it returns false, the lock was free, and now it is held.

tas3.text: Leaving, the process sets the lock back to false.

mutex.text: Programmers use a friendlier tool built on top: the mutex lock. Acquire before the critical section. Release after.

mutex2.text: Five threads, each doing count plus plus inside the lock. The count always ends at five.

spin.text: If waiting means looping, the lock is a spinlock. The waiting thread burns CPU doing nothing.

sem.text: A semaphore is an integer, S, touched only by two atomic operations: wait, and signal.

sem1.text: Think of S as the number of free resources. Here, three.

sem2.text: wait takes one. One, two, three processes take one each. S is zero.

sem3.text: A fourth calls wait. S drops to minus one, and it sleeps in the semaphore's queue. A negative S counts the sleepers.

sem4.text: When a process calls signal, S goes up by one, and one sleeper wakes.

bin.text: A semaphore that is only zero or one works like a mutex. The difference: a mutex has an owner. Only the thread that locked it may unlock it.

ord.text: Semaphores can also force an order. Start synch at zero. P two calls wait, and sleeps.

ord2.text: P one runs S one, then signals. Only now can P two run S two. S one always comes first.

dead.text: But locks can trap you. P zero takes S, then Q. P one takes Q, then S.

dead2.text: Each holds one lock, and waits for the other's. Neither lets go. That is deadlock.

fix.text: The fix: take the locks in the same order everywhere.

more.text: Two more failures. Starvation: one process never gets its turn. Priority inversion: a low priority process holds a lock that a high priority one needs.

ex1.text: test and set is one atomic step.

ex4.text: synch at zero forces an order.
